description: Reads PCAP Next Generation files and generates CLR objects from its data. Implemented according to the draft specification at https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng/.
releaseNotes:
* Port to .NET 10.0. Breaking: .NET 5 through 9 are no longer targeted.
      * Add XML documentation for the public API.
      * Fix block options never being read, so option properties (interface name, packet flags, statistics, etc.) are now populated.
      * Fix crash when reading a packet hash option.
      * Fix IPv6 name resolution records being read as 8 bytes instead of 16.
      * Fix link layer error flags reading the wrong bits.
      * Fix interface statistics timestamps and Packet Block padding.
      * Support big-endian sections, including files mixing both byte orders (#4).
      * Support unseekable streams; Reset requires a seekable stream (#5).
      * Skip unsupported block types (e.g. Custom and Decryption Secrets Blocks) and name resolution record types instead of throwing.
      * Fix Reader(string) failing on read-only files.
      * Support base-2 timestamp resolutions and apply if_tsoffset in EnhancedPacketBlock.GetTimestamp, which now returns UTC and reports precision loss per timestamp.
      * Fix interfaces without if_tsresol defaulting to a resolution of seconds instead of microseconds.
      * Skip sections whose major version isn't 1.
      * End option strings at a zero byte, and skip options with an invalid length, listing them in InvalidOptionCodes.
      * Keep every value of repeatable options (Comments, IPv4Addresses, IPv6Addresses, Hashes); the singular properties return the first.
      * Add custom options, the Toeplitz hash algorithm, if_hardware, if_txspeed, if_rxspeed, if_iana_tzname, epb_packetid, epb_queue, epb_verdict, epb_processid_threadid, packet flag bits 9-11, and EUI-48/EUI-64 name resolution records.
      * Fix SimplePacketBlock.Data including padding; its length now honors the first interface's snap length.
      * Breaking: PacketBlock.Timestamp is now the raw timestamp, with GetTimestamp to convert it, as in EnhancedPacketBlock.
      * Add GetTimestamp, GetStartTime and GetEndTime to InterfaceStatisticsBlock.
